extracted.intended_audience: general readers and researchers interested in Philippine politics, online media, and the Mocha Uson Blog
extracted.subtask_short: wiki article about Mocha Uson Blog
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article summarizing the history, content, controversies, reception, and technical/platform details of the Mocha Uson Blog (a Filipino political blog/Facebook page). Intended to document factual and contextual information about the site and its public impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of site / platform status
rubrics_metrics.description: Type of site: Facebook Page / Blog. Current status: Active. 'A former standalone blog site, it is currently a Facebook page, after www.mocha.com.ph went defunct in February 2017.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to classify the publication medium and whether the original blog remains online; important for understanding where content is hosted and how users access it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language availability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the languages in which the blog publishes content or has presence; relevant for audience reach and content analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership and authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner: Mocha Productions. Created by: Mocha Uson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies who controls the site and who is responsible for content/voice; useful for attribution and conflicts-of-interest assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Launch / history timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Launched: Blog site: 2006. History notes: previously sexual-content focused, later transitioned to political advocacy around the 2016 presidential campaign; blog site defunct by February 2017; mobile app released January 2018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chronological markers documenting the blog's evolution and major platform changes; important for contextualizing content shifts and claims about influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content focus / thematic evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Mocha Uson Blog previously concentrated on giving sex-related tips or advice and featured 'sessions in the bedroom' with the Mocha Girls. It later became a platform for Filipinos to express concerns and became an online political advocacy tool to promote the 2016 presidential campaign of Rodrigo Duterte.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes topical scope and any major pivot in subject matter; useful when evaluating editorial intent and audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable posts / controversies as evaluative examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Pepederalismo: August 2018 video 'Pepedederalismo' criticized as lewd and obscene; Disrespecting sign language: September 2018 video drew flak for making fun of sign language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific controversial items used as case studies of problematic content; these examples indicate types of content that generate public criticism and inform reputational assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile application details
rubrics_metrics.description: Developer: Cloud Panda PH. Initial release: 2017. Stable release 1.2 (2 November 2017). Operating system: iOS, Android. App features: allows users to post videos, text, and access features such as Mocha TV, DDS Podcast, and OFW Help.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical and feature information important for assessing distribution channels and interactive capabilities of the blog beyond the Facebook page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience reach / engagement metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: The Facebook page's followers increased to 4 million after Uson became a vocal supporter of President Rodrigo Duterte; the then-defunct blog site had 20 million hits in 2016; mobile app downloaded more than 10,000 times as of 2018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative indicators of reach and popularity used to measure influence and the scale of the blog's audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reception and criticism / perceived bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics: Vincent Lazatin (Transparency and Accountability Network) criticized the blog for polarizing content; Maria Ressa (Rappler) criticized it as a pro-Duterte propaganda tool that 'takes advantage of Facebook algorithm'. A Change.org petition sought removal from Facebook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarizes prominent critiques alleging bias, manipulation of platforms, or polarizing effects — useful when evaluating credibility and political alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searchability / platform enforcement incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: As of March 20, 2020, the blog was not searchable on Facebook; hashtag #MochaUsonisOverParty trended as users sought to mass report the blog; the page later resurfaced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents incidents where platform actions or mass reporting affected visibility; relevant to assessments of platform moderation and the blog's resilience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archival / domain status
rubrics_metrics.description: As of 22 September 2021, the website was set up to redirect to a Twitter account with the handle @PhilippinesPHP, with the domain name taken over by another unconnected entity per its WHOIS record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates domain change or takeover; relevant when tracing provenance of content or verifying primary sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article maintenance note
rubrics_metrics.description: This article needs to be updated. The reason given is: conflicting info about the blog's status. (August 2021)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metadata flag that signals the Wikipedia page itself may be out of date or contain conflicting information — important caution for users relying on the article for current status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorization / labeling (e.g., 'Fake news', 'promotional tone')
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories include: Facebook pages, Philippine blogs, IOS software, Android software, Asian political websites, Philippine websites, Politics of the Philippines, Fake news. Hidden categories note 'All articles with dead external links' and 'All articles with a promotional tone'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labels and categories assigned by Wikipedia editors that summarize perceived attributes of the site (e.g., association with 'fake news' or 'promotional tone'); these act as evaluative metadata for readers.
